changes: BREAKING: JSON-only normative bundle.
Added deterministic routing + persisted RouteDecision.
Strengthened webhook tenant-binding rules.
Made failover safety and ambiguous-state behavior explicit.
ENTERPRISE HARDENING - parity with PAY-1 v2.5.0
Upgraded to CS-0@2.2.0 schema and BP-0 bundle structure.
Added core_domain_contract with Ash 3.x identities.
Implemented binary circuit breaker with OBS-1 integration.
Added correlation tracking and decision_hash.
Webhook hardening: HMAC+timestamp, storm detection.
Complete telemetry contract with Ash.Tracer.
Two-tier anomaly detection.
CRITICAL OPERATIONAL HARDENING - addresses circuit breaker deadlock and webhook performance.
FIX 1: Fractional traffic shedding (5% probationary throttle) replaces binary circuit breakers.
FIX 2: Optimistic webhook processing with selective fetch for high-value events only.
FIX 3: Independent hash verification in reconciliation using clean-room implementation.
FIX 4: UnboundWebhookEvent holding pen for orphaned webhooks failing tenant-binding.
FIX 5: Real-time failover rate monitoring (5-minute SEV2) replaces daily aggregate.
Added probationary_throttle state (5% traffic) for degraded providers.
Added cascade prevention logic when all providers degrade simultaneously.
Added selective fetch triggers: refunds, high-value captures (>$1000), disputes.
Added independent decision_hash verification algorithm specification.
Added 24-hour TTL and retry strategy for unbound webhooks.
Moved failover spike detection from daily to 5-minute real-time SEV2 alert.
Added 5 new P0/P1 rules addressing operational rigidity.
BREAKING: Normalized tenant key from org_id (uuid) → org_id (string) per TEN-1 v1.6.8 canonical model.
DEPENDENCY ALIGNMENT: Upgraded TEN-1 min_version from 1.5.0 → 1.6.8.
DEPENDENCY ALIGNMENT: Upgraded LED-1 min_version from 2.1.0 → 2.3.4 for org_id/RLS alignment.
DEPENDENCY ALIGNMENT: Upgraded PAY-1 min_version from 2.5.0 → 2.6.0.
Removed org_id from routing model recommended inputs (org_id is the canonical tenant key).
Updated idempotency key format to reference org_id instead of org_id.
Updated telemetry span attributes: pay2.org_id → pay2.org_id.
Updated all resource attributes (RouteDecision, RoutePolicy, ProviderAccount, ProviderWebhookEvent) to use org_id.
Updated required identities to reference org_id.
Migration: Existing implementations must rename org_id columns/fields to org_id and update type from uuid to string.
DOC: ERR-1 canonical section text no longer includes alias code strings (avoids accidental regex matches).
FIX: summary normalized to a string per CS-0 contract schema; detailed object moved to executive_summary.
FIX: ERR-1 top-level error codes now use canonical underscore forms (ERR_FORBIDDEN, ERR_UNAVAILABLE, ERR_BAD_REQUEST, ERR_CONFLICT).
FIX: Reconciliation mismatch subcode now uses registered, namespaced subcode PAY_ROUTE_DECISION_HASH_MISMATCH (requires ERR-1 update).
FIX: Tenant-scoped RoutePolicy and ProviderAccount now require non-null org_id (no implicit platform scope via nullable org_id).
FIX: Removed platform-scope wording from RoutePolicy purpose (tenant-scoped only).
HARDENING: Decision hash verification now specifies canonical encodings and uses length-prefixed encoding (delimiter ambiguity forbidden).
HARDENING: Clean-room hash computation enforcement now specifies required module + forbidden dependency edge (NEW proposed governance lint rule).
PACKAGING: Bundle normalized to BP-0 foldered bundle structure with regenerated manifest.

Dependency floor bump: ERR-1>=1.4.2 to match suite-wide PAY_REFERENCE_* subcode registry used by canonical money confirmation seam.

Add dependency_pins.gc_001_chain and register required ERR-1 subcode PAY_LATE_CAPTURE_AFTER_HOLD_EXPIRED.
Bump dependency floors: ERR-1>=1.4.15, PAY-1>=2.7.5, ORD-1>=3.5.0, add PAY-3>=2.9.2.

Trusted config mapping provider accounts to tenants, currencies, regions.

Context/type safety only; PAY-2 is a router (emits_events=false, outbox_events=[]).
Ledger posting boundaries with org_id alignment; routing must not imply posting.
Queue taxonomy for webhook ingestion and reconciliation workers.

Webhook signature verification, replay protections, secrets.
Tenant isolation with canonical org_id key and 'hide existence' semantics.
TG-0 v2.3.0 gate standard: denial tests + runtime verification primitives + harness interlock.
Seat allocation and hold state must be interpreted consistently for payment authorization, capture, and dispute workflows.

executive_summary.one_liner: Provider routing and reconciliation contract with deterministic selection, denial semantics, idempotency, and decision-hash verification for auditability.
executive_summary.problem: Multi-PSP routing becomes a money-loss machine when selection is non-deterministic, circuit breakers cause cascade failures, or webhook verification doubles latency during storms.
executive_summary.solution: Routing policy with immutable RouteDecision, fractional traffic shedding (5% probationary throttle), optimistic webhook processing for trusted signatures, independent hash verification, orphaned webhook holding pen, and 5-minute failover spike detection.

hard_rules: Failover MUST NOT create duplicates: no second capture/authorization unless first is proven non-effective.
Failover requires provider truth check when state is ambiguous (timeouts, unknown capture state).
If any attempt might have succeeded, system MUST enter pending and reconcile before fulfillment.
Circuit breaker MUST exclude providers with open circuits from failover routing.

GC-001.notes: PAY-2 webhook ingestion/routing remains tentative; money finality is verified via PAY-1 only. Upon verified money confirmation, PAY-2 MUST trigger ORD-1 reconciliation; if ORD indicates grace/holds expired, PAY-2 MUST initiate PAY-3 compensation and emit OBS signals with ERR-1 subcode.

changed_params_same_key_behavior.client_guidance: Parameters changed; derive new idempotency key for new routing attempt.

key_requirements.description: Keys MUST be context-derived and MUST be reused for retry of same routing operation.

p0.text: Webhook durability dedupe identity MUST include provider_account_ref. Uniqueness tuple is (provider_id, provider_account_ref, provider_event_id).

clean_room_implementation.description: Reconciliation worker MUST re-calculate decision_hash using independent implementation, not calling RouteDecision.compute_decision_hash.

enforcement.notes: NEW: proposed invariant — requires LINT-0 rule to forbid dependency edge CleanRoomHash -> RouteDecision.

verification_logic.description: Reconciliation MUST independently compute the decision_hash as SHA256 over the ordered fields using the canonicalization and length-prefixed encoding rules above. Delimiter-based concatenation is FORBIDDEN.

gc_001.description: GC-001 late money confirmation handling: translate tentative provider events into PAY-1 verification, then ORD reconciliation; compensate via PAY-3 when money arrives after order grace/holds expired.
workflow_steps: Persist webhook event with signature proof + tenant binding (or holding pen) and correlate to RouteDecision/payment_intent_id/v42_correlation_id when available.
For any webhook that indicates potential finality (capture/paid/settled), enqueue PAY-1.verify_payment_reference using provider_reference_id and payment_reference_c14n for correlation only.
Only after PAY-1 verification attests paid_confirmed_at_utc + verified_payment_attempt_id + evidence_digest_sha256 may PAY-2 emit money-confirmed event for downstream consumption.
Trigger ORD-1 reconciliation using v42_correlation_id + verified_payment_attempt_id + paid_confirmed_at_utc; ORD decides whether order is still within grace and whether seats/holds are still valid.
If ORD rejects as expired or holds released, PAY-2 MUST initiate PAY-3 compensation (prefer void; fallback refund) and record ERR-1 error_subcode PAY_LATE_CAPTURE_AFTER_HOLD_EXPIRED.

trust_rules: Inputs MUST be derived from persisted Order/Invoice resources inside tenant scope.
Any client-provided field used by routing MUST be validated against server truth or ignored.

policy_versioning.reason: Changing routing rules without versioning makes reconciliation impossible.

rules.rationale: Non-deterministic routing breaks reconciliation and causes double-charges during retries.
rules.text: Routing MUST be deterministic and auditable: same trusted inputs + same policy version => same route. RouteDecisions MUST be persisted.

rules.rationale: Misrouting webhooks is a direct cross-tenant money movement risk.
rules.text: Tenant binding for webhooks and routing MUST NOT rely on untrusted inputs. Cross-tenant access MUST be hidden (ERR_NOT_FOUND) per TEN-1.

rules.rationale: Failover without truth checks causes double-charges.
rules.text: Failover MUST NOT create duplicate authorizations/captures. Any ambiguous state MUST transition to pending and block fulfillment until reconciled.

rules.rationale: Client/network retries must not produce different routes or provider attempts.
rules.text: All route creation actions MUST be idempotent and parameter-consistent. Replays with same key but different inputs MUST be rejected.

rules.rationale: Enables correlation from order → routing → adapter → PSP → reconciliation.
rules.text: RouteDecision MUST persist v42_correlation_id from ORD-1 and decision_hash for end-to-end audit trail.

rules.rationale: Prevents reconciliation errors from tampered or race-condition RouteDecisions.
rules.text: Reconciliation MUST verify decision_hash before applying provider state changes to prevent tampering.

rules.rationale: Ensures audit trail integrity and prevents tampering.
rules.text: RouteDecision and RoutePolicy resources MUST be immutable: create+read only, no update/destroy actions.

rules.rationale: Prevents cascade failures when multiple providers degrade simultaneously; binary circuit breakers cause total blackout.
rules.text: Circuit breaker MUST implement fractional traffic shedding: healthy (100%), degraded (50%), probationary_throttle (5%), circuit_open (0%).

rules.rationale: Integrates circuit breaker state with routing decisions.
rules.text: Routing MUST query OBS-1 provider health status before selection; providers with open circuits MUST be excluded.

rules.rationale: Prevents replay attacks and stale webhook processing.
rules.text: Webhooks MUST be HMAC-verified with timestamp check; reject payloads older than 300 seconds.

rules.rationale: Protects reconciliation workers from replay storm DDoS.
rules.text: If webhook rate exceeds 10× baseline, emit payment.webhook_replay_storm_detected.v1 and throttle ingestion.

rules.rationale: Defends against webhook spoofing and ensures state consistency.
rules.text: For critical state transitions, implement fetch-before-process: call PSP API to verify event before state change.

rules.rationale: Enables performance monitoring and anomaly detection.
rules.text: All routing actions MUST be instrumented with Ash.Tracer spans including org_id, provider_id, route_policy_version, reason_code.

rules.rationale: Zero-cost compile-time redaction prevents secret leakage.
rules.text: RoutePolicy and ProviderAccount MUST derive Inspect using :only/:except to exclude secrets from logs.

rules.rationale: Prevents maintenance-driven log leaks.
rules.text: CI MUST fail if new field matching sensitive patterns added to routing resources without Inspect exclusion.

rules.rationale: Detects routing anomalies from config errors or provider outages.
rules.text: Monitor routing distribution: alert if one provider share shifts >40% in 15 minutes.

rules.rationale: Daily monitoring is too slow; real-time detection prevents silent failover cost leakage.
rules.text: Monitor failover rate in real-time: fire SEV2 if 5-minute rate exceeds 3× 24-hour baseline. Daily aggregate for trend analysis.

rules.rationale: Prevents repeated failures from misconfigured ProviderAccounts.
rules.text: If RouteDecision fails >3 times in 60 minutes, mark poisoned, emit alert, and trigger automatic re-routing with provider exclusion.

rules.rationale: Prevents circuit breaker deadlock where all providers trip simultaneously during traffic spikes.
rules.text: A health-degraded provider MUST NOT be fully excluded; it MUST move to probationary_throttle (5% traffic) for automated recovery testing.

rules.rationale: Prevents fetch-before-process from doubling latency and overwhelming worker capacity during webhook storms.
rules.text: Optimistic processing MUST be enabled for HMAC-verified webhooks; hard fetch ONLY for high-value events (refunds, >$1000 captures, disputes).

rules.rationale: Prevents bugs in hash logic from being invisible; ensures independent verification.
rules.text: Reconciliation MUST re-calculate decision_hash using independent clean-room implementation, not RouteDecision.compute_decision_hash.

rules.rationale: Prevents payment loss from webhooks arriving before parent RouteDecision due to replication lag.
rules.text: Webhooks failing tenant-binding MUST be persisted in UnboundWebhookEvent holding pen and retried for 24 hours with exponential backoff.

rules.rationale: Prevents silent failover to high-fee providers from burning profit margin for hours.
rules.text: Failover rate spike MUST trigger SEV2 alert if 5-minute rate exceeds 3× 24-hour baseline.

rules.rationale: Enables SRE to detect provider outages and routing anomalies.
rules.text: Every route decision MUST emit structured log/metric with org_id, provider_id, route_policy_version, reason_code (no PII).

rules.rationale: Prevents adapter/provider-specific interpretation drift and blocks ticket issuance on non-final money states.
rules.text: PAY-2 MUST NOT attest or derive money finality (paid_confirmed) for fulfillment. Money finality MUST be attested exclusively by PAY-1.verify_payment_reference producing verified_payment_attempt_id + paid_confirmed_at_utc + evidence_digest_sha256.

rules.rationale: Stops 'fast-ack' webhook handling from becoming an implicit payment confirmation seam.
rules.text: Optimistic webhook processing MAY mark events as tentative, but tentative events MUST NOT trigger fulfillment, ticket issuance, or refund eligibility decisions. Tentative events MUST set requires_truth_check=true and MUST enqueue provider truth reconciliation before any downstream money_confirmed action.

rules.rationale: Avoids double-charges and prevents fulfillment on unknown/ambiguous state.
rules.text: On ambiguous provider state (timeouts, unknown capture/settlement), PAY-2 MUST enter pending and block fulfillment until provider truth reconciliation completes. Reconciliation MUST feed PAY-1.verify_payment_reference to obtain canonical money confirmation proof when applicable.

rules.details: PAY-2 MUST compute payment_reference_c14n as: 'payref_c14n/v1:' + provider + ':' + sha256_hex(provider_reference_id). PAY-2 MUST treat payment_reference_c14n as correlation-only and MUST NOT use it as a verification lookup key.

rules.rationale: Provider webhooks are not authoritative for money finality; GC-001 requires PAY-1 verification and evidence binding to avoid zombie fulfillment after holds expire.
rules.text: On any webhook event that indicates potential money finality (capture/paid/settled), PAY-2 MUST enqueue PAY-1.verify_payment_reference and MUST treat the webhook as tentative until PAY-1 returns verified_payment_attempt_id + paid_confirmed_at_utc + evidence_digest_sha256.

rules.rationale: Money arriving after checkout expiry must not resurrect inventory/fulfillment; compensation is mandatory to preserve seat truth and ledger correctness.
rules.text: After PAY-1 attests paid_confirmed, PAY-2 MUST trigger ORD-1 reconciliation. If ORD indicates order grace expired or holds released, PAY-2 MUST initiate PAY-3 compensation (prefer void; fallback refund) and MUST use ERR-1 error_subcode PAY_LATE_CAPTURE_AFTER_HOLD_EXPIRED for audit + alerting.

sections.text: All public error envelopes MUST emit ERR-1 primary codes WITH underscores (e.g., ERR_BAD_REQUEST, ERR_CONFLICT) and MUST NOT emit alias forms without underscores.
